records.claim: Corn–soybean is a documented common Iowa row-crop sequence.
records.applicability: Central Iowa row-crop exploration, not proof of an individual field's history or performance.
records.limitations: Common practice does not imply best practice.

records.claim: Iowa beginner guidance places fall cereal rye after corn before soybean.
records.applicability: Corn-to-soybean systems with an actual fall establishment and spring termination plan.
records.limitations: Weather, herbicide, equipment, and local timing may prevent fit.

records.claim: Iowa beginner guidance uses winter-killed oats after soybean before corn.
records.applicability: Soybean-to-corn system with an early enough fall establishment window.
records.limitations: Winter-killed oats do not provide living spring cover.

records.claim: An oat/alfalfa–alfalfa–corn–soybean rotation was studied in the Upper Midwest.
records.applicability: Only an exploration pattern for farms able to use perennial forage and small grains.
records.limitations: Minnesota findings may not transfer to this Iowa field; economics unverified.

records.claim: Winter cereal rye ahead of corn can create establishment and seedling-disease risks if termination is poorly timed.
records.limitations: Risk depends on weather, termination, and planting management.

records.claim: SSURGO map units may contain multiple components and do not replace a field soil test.
records.limitations: Point lookup and component percentages are spatial estimates, not samples.

records.claim: NASA POWER and GPM IMERG provide gridded precipitation context at different spatial and temporal scales.
records.applicability: A requested point with valid dataset responses.
records.limitations: Do not infer soil moisture, field rainfall, or a forecast from either product. IMERG run and units require request-level checks.

records.claim: Cover crops add seed, application, and termination costs that must be compared with locally plausible benefits.
records.applicability: Iowa cover-crop exploration; actual costs depend on the operation and year.
records.limitations: No dollar amount, net return, or payback is established for the user's field.

records.claim: Deep-rooted forage legumes such as alfalfa may leave less subsoil moisture for a following grain crop under dry conditions.
records.applicability: Upper Midwest diversified rotations under dry conditions; use only as a question for Iowa fields.
records.limitations: The Minnesota extension summary does not quantify this risk for the requested field or climate period.
